newsitem.title: USA: SPX says 1996 oper earnings above estimates.
newsitem.headline: SPX says 1996 oper earnings above estimates.

text.p: SPX Corp said Monday its operating earnings before non-recurring charges of $1.76 a share in 1996 exceeded analysts expectations.

SPX reported a net loss in 1996 of $62.3 million or $4.45 a share, including a $67.8 million or $4.85 a share writeoff of goodwill from its former Automotive Diagnostics division, $12.4 million or $0.89 a share restructuring charge and $6.6 million or $0.47 a share extraordinary loss from repurchasing notes.

In 1995, it had a net loss of $5.3 million or $0.40 a share, after a $10,724,000 restructuring charge and goodwill writeoff, a $2,847,000 or $0.22 a share loss from discontinued operations and $1,078,000 or $0.08 a share extraordinary loss.

SPX said its decision to write off Automotive Diagnostics' goodwill resulted from a strategic review completed in December. The company said the business, as it was purchased, would not generate returns necessary to support the recorded goodwill.
"Looking at 1997, we are confident the company will complete another year of improved performance," John Blystone, chairman, said in a statement.
